tasks.design: The clerk reads open times, agrees the mortgage closing with the people involved, and conducts it in person. They note what they conducted. The closing is not recorded. Agreeing the time stays a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding a time everyone could make was the hard part, and the closing itself was the work.
tasks.enabler_now: A calendar can show openings. Conducting the closing stays in the room.
tasks.still_hard: The closing conversation, the documents signed there, and the exceptions stay with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk schedules and conducts the closing. A calendar does not conduct it.
tasks.altitude: Conducting the closing stays in full. Scheduling stays a conversation. Only reading open times is shorter.

reach.task: Attend the closing the clerk conducts
reach.learn: The closing is not a recording

evidence.claim: A calendar can show open times. Scheduling with the parties, and conducting the closing, stay with the person. The closing is not recorded.

National rules differ on recording calls and on monitoring staff. This design does not record a call and does not score the clerk. A bot that spoke to a customer would have to say it is a machine. This design has no bot.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a closing needs a time and ends when the clerk has conducted it. They schedule and conduct. The room is not recorded.
The field is an open time. The calendar produces it. The clerk produces the agreement and conducts the closing. If people cannot make the time, they keep talking.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree the closing stays.
unknowns: Whether the parties share a calendar the clerk can read.
Who else must be in the room to conduct the closing.
research_questions: Do the parties share a calendar the clerk can read?
Who else must be in the room to conduct the closing?

tasks.short: Review whether payments and terms are followed.

steps.what: List accounts whose payments are late.
Review customer accounts that are late.
Determine whether other terms are followed.

tasks.design: The loan screen lists accounts whose paid date is after the due date. The clerk reviews those accounts and determines whether other terms are followed. They accept that review. {DOCS} files that version. No letter and no default are sent from this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Late accounts were found by scanning a list, and other terms were a separate reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Due date and paid date can already show a late payment. Other terms are still a judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Insurance, occupancy, and any term that is not a date stay with the clerk. Nothing here declares a default.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk reviews the accounts and determines the other terms. The list only compares two dates.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still reviews late accounts and determines whether other terms are followed. The file is their review. It is not a default notice.

reach.task: Read a review the clerk accepted
reach.learn: The review is not a demand

evidence.claim: Comparing a due date with a paid date can list a late account. Deciding whether other loan terms are followed stays with the person. The list is not an adverse action.

A decision on credit that has a legal effect on a person must not be taken by a system alone. A person decides. This design does not score an applicant, does not set a credit limit, and does not grant an extension.

assumptions: The workflow starts when payments are due and ends when the accepted review is on file. The clerk determines the other terms. No notice is sent.

The fields are the due date, the paid date, and their acceptance of the review. The loan record produces the dates. The clerk produces the review. If a date is blank, the account is not listed as late.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps agree the date comparison can move. They disagree that other terms, or a default, can be decided by the list.
unknowns: Whether due date and paid date are already stored.
Which other terms are not dates and must be read by the clerk.
research_questions: Are due date and paid date already stored?
Which other terms are not dates and must be read by the clerk?

tasks.short: Establish credit limits and grant extensions.
tasks.design: The clerk establishes the credit limit and grants any extension, including on an overdue account. A system does not set the limit, does not grant the extension, and does not score the customer. The clerk writes the figure themselves.
tasks.previous_blocker: It was tempting to let a score set the limit. The decision is the clerk's.
tasks.enabler_now: There is no new tool. The decision stays manual because it has a legal effect.
tasks.still_hard: The limit and the extension are judgements about this customer. They stay with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk establishes the limit and grants the extension. Nothing else does.
tasks.altitude: The limit and the extension stay in full with the clerk. No time moves.

reach.task: Receive a limit the clerk established
reach.learn: A screen does not set it

evidence.claim: A decision on credit that has a legal effect on a person must not be taken by a system alone. A person decides. This design does not score an applicant, does not set a credit limit, and does not grant an extension.
Setting a credit limit or granting an extension is the decision. It stays with a person even when the account history is on a screen.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a limit or an extension is asked and ends when the clerk has decided. Nothing is calculated into a decision. Zero incremental hours are justified because no new tool and no new check are added.
The clerk produces the limit and the extension. There is no new field and no score.
The prior classes this task as human. The steps agree.
unknowns: Whether national rules require a second person for a limit above a threshold.
Which overdue accounts this clerk is allowed to extend.
research_questions: Do national rules require a second person for a limit above a threshold?

tasks.short: Calculate interest and correct the errors.

steps.what: Calculate principal and payment from those fields.
Calculate closing costs from those fields.
Review errors on interest and payment.

tasks.design: The loan screen's own calculation of interest, principal, payment, and closing costs is tried first, using only stated fields. The clerk reviews errors and corrects them, then accepts the figures. {ERP} writes that version. A wrong input is not silently replaced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The figures were worked on a calculator and typed back, and an error was found late.
tasks.enabler_now: The loan screen should already calculate interest from principal, rate, and days. That is tried before any new arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: An error that is not a arithmetic slip, such as a wrong rate, still has to be corrected by the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk reviews, corrects, and accepts the figures. The screen only calculates stated fields.
tasks.altitude: The clerk still reviews errors and accepts the corrected interest before it is written. The calculation does not change a rate or a principal the record does not hold.

reach.task: Use interest figures the clerk accepted
reach.learn: A calculated figure is not accepted until the clerk says so

evidence.claim: Interest, principal, payment, and closing costs from stated fields are arithmetic. The person still reviews errors and corrects a figure the arithmetic got wrong or that rested on a bad input.
Consumer-credit rules require a person to be able to intervene in an automated check of credit and to explain the result. Interest here is arithmetic on stated fields. It is not a credit decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the inputs are on the record and ends when the accepted figures are written. The clerk corrects errors. The screen uses stated fields only.

The fields are the principal, the rate, the term, the days, the cost inputs, and their acceptance. The loan record produces the inputs. The clerk produces the correction. If an input is blank, that figure is not calculated.
The prior classes this task as automate. The steps agree the arithmetic can move. They disagree that a correction can be written before the clerk accepts it.
unknowns: Whether the loan screen already calculates interest from those fields.
Which closing costs are not a formula and must stay with the clerk.
research_questions: Does the loan screen already calculate interest from those fields?

role.ambitious_version: Every credit limit is one the clerk set, and every interest figure that is written is one they accepted.
